cartographer.declared_question: Which execution assumptions belong inside a generative plate, and which should remain replaceable properties of a reader?
cartographer.inquiry_basis: Existing WebAssembly proposals REL-P-000010 and REL-P-000011 and exact FN-33.

sources_checked.attribution: W3C WebAssembly Working Group, WebAssembly Core Specification, introduction, scope, security considerations, and embedder overview.
source_facts: Both the cited August draft and today's canonical draft describe portable low-level computation without Web-specific assumptions.
The core defines instructions, binary encoding, validation, and execution semantics, while complementary embedding APIs define environmental interaction and invocation.
Environmental I/O and resource access depend on functions provided by the embedder and imported into the module; policies and hardware side-channel mitigations remain embedding responsibilities.
The canonical document is a Candidate Recommendation Draft dated October 23, not a claim of W3C endorsement or a finished Recommendation.
sources_checked.inference: The portable-computation and explicit-host boundary remains technically adjacent to FN-33's replaceable reader. It is not preservation of artistic assets, presentation, timing, randomness, authorized edition lineage, or deterministic visual behavior.
sources_checked.uncertainty: Bounded document comparison, not a runtime trial, implementation security audit, or guarantee of reconstruction. No endorsement, partnership, or collaboration is implied.
sources_checked.access_note: The canonical document exceeded the web reader's size limit and was read through a read-only HTTP download, alongside the dated source already cited by the proposal. Two guessed split-document paths returned 404; the actual canonical and cited dated documents were available. Their supported boundary claims agree.
